title: Potential for replacing hospitalization in geriatric patients through General Practitioner (GP)-led hospital at home care- a study protocol of an explorative study from perspectives of patients, relatives and GPs
summary: Geriatric patients (patients with age-related illnesses) are disproportionately affected by avoidable hospital stays, which are associated with significant health risks, stress and high costs. The internationally established ‘Hospital at Home’ (HaH) care model offers a potentially effective and patient-centred alternative to inpatient care by enabling medically and nursing-supervised treatment in the home environment, characterised by close monitoring and, where necessary, telemedical support. HaH has hardly been implemented in Germany to date, which is why the planned project aims to investigate the potential of (GP-led) HaH models with the involvement of key stakeholders.
conditions: The patient has had at least one hospitalization with a geriatric indication in the last 6 months.

interventions.name:
Study Part 1: Literature Review
•	Objectives: To explore feasibility and effectiveness of GP led HaH models from internation research literature. Exploration of the topic “(GP led) HaH for geriatric patients”; systematic synthesis of the current state of research; foundation for developing the data

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Dyadic Interviews with Patient and Family member/Caregiver:
•	The patient and a family member/caregiver are able to give their consent for participating data collection.
•	The patient has had at least one hospitalization with a geriatric indication in the last 6 months.
•	The patient and the family member/caregiver have sufficient language skills to conduct the interview (interview language: German).
•	The patient agrees to an expert interview between the researchers with their GP.

Expert interviews  with GPs:
•	The GP has treated the patients, who would like to participate in the dyadic interviews, in the last 6 months.
•	The patient has given their consent for their GP to conduct an expert interview about their medical history.
Exclusion criteria:
Dyadic Interviews with Patient and Family member/Caregiver:
•	The patient and/or their family member/caregiver are not capable of giving informed consent.
•	The patient has not been hospitalized for geriatric reasons in the last 6 months.
•	The patient and family member/caregiver do not have sufficient language skills to conduct the interview (interview language: German)
•	The patient does not consent to an expert interview with their GP.

Expert interviews  with GPs:
•	The GP has not treated the patients, who would like to participate in the dyadic interviews, in the last 6 months.
•	The patient did not give their consent for their GP to conduct an expert interview about their medical history.
